Good morning, everyone. I am Daniel Ross, and I coordinate international programs at a trade association in Toronto. Juliana, would you like to start?
Sure. Good morning, Daniel. I am Juliana, and I am a coordinator at the Brazil-Canada Chamber of Commerce.
Nice to meet you. And what do you do there, exactly?
I work with partnerships and commercial contacts. I am the point of contact for many member companies.
Great. And what are you working on at the moment?
At the moment we are preparing a partnership with associations in Canada. That is why I reached out to you.
Perfect. I am in charge of our Brazil program, and my colleague Emma is based in Vancouver. She joins our calls every two weeks.

I host a lot of international calls, and I always start the same way. We do a quick round, about thirty seconds for each person. There are often ten or twelve people on the call, from four or five countries, so time is important. The problem I hear most often is simple. People say only their job title. Coordinator, manager, director. But a title means different things in different countries. So I ask for three things. First, your name. Second, what you do, in normal words. And third, what you are working on now, this week or this month. When people do that, everybody knows who to talk to after the call.

I am a trade officer, and I am based in Ottawa. In general, I help Canadian companies find partners in Latin America. That is my job, every year. But on a call, people usually want to know something else. They want to know what I am doing now. And this month I am organizing a visit of five Canadian companies to Sao Paulo. We are planning meetings with Brazilian companies and with the chamber of commerce. So I always say both things. My job explains why I am on the call. My current project explains what you can ask me about after the call.

Welcome to the chamber, and thank you for becoming a member company. This short message explains how we work. A chamber of commerce connects companies from two countries. We organize events, we introduce companies to possible partners, and we share information about the market. Every new member has a point of contact on our team. Your point of contact is the first person you talk to, about anything. Our advice is simple. In your first month, reach out to your point of contact and tell us what you are working on. When we know your plans, we can find the right partners for you.
